references.title: A2: Analog Malicious Hardware
references.venue: 2016 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
notes: Fabrication-time attacker modifies an otherwise trusted placed-and-routed design.
Charge accumulation from unusually frequent toggles of a normally quiet wire crosses a threshold; leakage resets charge between infrequent toggles.
Demonstrated with fabricated OR1200 processor and privilege-bit payload. A toy RC/behavioral trigger is A2-inspired, not a silicon reproduction.

references.title: SPICED: Syntactical Bug and Trojan Pattern Identification in A/MS Circuits using LLM-Enhanced Detection
references.venue: Accepted at PAINE 2024; arXiv version verified
notes: Original experiments use GPT-3.5-turbo, HSPICE voltage/current logs, specifications and few-shot anomaly rules.
Rules inspect output specification violations, intermediate-node voltage deviations and MOSFET current anomalies.
Reported average Trojan component coverage 93.32% and impacted-node true-positive rate 93.4%. These are not a clean-netlist false-positive rate.
A netlist-only, zero-shot classifier must be called SPICED-inspired rather than a reproduction.

references.title: LATENT: LLM-Augmented Trojan Insertion and Evaluation Framework for Analog Netlist Topologies
references.venue: Accepted for presentation at IEEE ICLAD 2025; arXiv version verified
notes: Uses GPT-4o-mini at temperature 0.3 for both attacker and reimplemented SPICED; HSPICE simulation.
Table I averages component-level evasion across 15 circuits: one-shot 23.7%, LATENT 94.4%. These are not attempt-level whole-netlist escape rates.
Sec IV-C printed intersection formula is a detection fraction, conflicting with prose interpreting 100% as evasion; report definition explicitly rather than copying the ambiguous equation.
Stops after 100% evasion for three consecutive iterations or component cap 0.6 times circuit node count.
Includes AMSNet circuits, op-amp, bandgap filter and LDO. Original SPICED code was unavailable to LATENT authors; they reimplemented it.
A binary-feedback condition is an additional ablation; LATENT Table I compares one-shot and its full iterative workflow.

analysis_recommendations: Freeze prompts, family bounds and validity thresholds before the main experiment; retain all failures.
Compare equal query budgets and number of attempts across none, binary and full conditions.
Count simulation failures and ineffective payloads as unsuccessful attempts; report conditional evasion among valid attacks separately.
Use repeated independent trajectories and describe within-trajectory dependence; do not claim each adaptive round is an independent sample.
Validate both dormant behavior and triggered malfunction; static truth-table success alone cannot validate a history-dependent trigger.
Report clean false positives using same detector, input normalization and prompt as attack evaluations.
Expected none < binary < full is a hypothesis, not an acceptance criterion.
Do not place LATENT component-level percentages as directly comparable benchmark bars beside whole-netlist attempt success.
